title: Telemetry batch
description:
The shape of both <prefix>/raw_batch (weight samples, grams) and <prefix>/rssi_batch (link RSSI, dBm). One entry per sampling loop iteration, so the two describe the same stretch of time -- but each batch is flushed and retried independently, so their counts need not match.

QoS 0: a publish that succeeds reached the transport, not the broker. Consumers must tolerate gaps, and `ts`/`duration_ms` rather than arrival order are the source of timing truth.

A batch is flushed when either telemetry.batch_entries is reached or the next value would push the payload past telemetry.batch_max_bytes, whichever comes first.

ts.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the FIRST entry of this batch was appended. Absent when the clock had not been set at that moment -- which is why it is absent rather than zero here: a consumer keying on it should skip the message, not place it in 1970.

duration_ms.description: Milliseconds from the first entry to the publish attempt. Divide by `count` to reconstruct per-sample times. Retained for consumers written against the predecessor, which published this and no absolute time at all.

count.description: Entries in `data`. Always equal to data.length; carried so a truncated message is detectable.

data.description: Weight samples to three decimal places, or RSSI as signed integers
